campbell.title: Campbell City Council — August 18, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a routine set of items including approval of past meeting minutes, payment of city bills, and a donation from the Campbell Police Foundation to support the K9 unit. The Council also took up two labor agreements covering police officers and carpenters, a review of the city's Measure O bond spending oversight, and administrative matters like designating conference delegates and a city clerk pay increase.
keyTopics: Acceptance of $41,911.62 in donations from the Campbell Police Foundation for K9 veterinary services and equipment
New labor agreements (2026-2028) with the Campbell Peace Officers Association and the North Coast States Carpenters Union
FY 2025 Annual Report from the Citizens' Bond Oversight Committee for Measure O
Designation of voting delegates for the League of California Cities Annual Conference
A merit pay increase for the City Clerk under an amended services agreement

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — August 19, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed a routine set of financial and administrative items, including check registers, a treasurer's report, and several service contracts for janitorial work, irrigation maintenance, and GIS consulting. The Council also considered a contested appeal over a proposed 25-lot subdivision on Pierce Road, along with park playground replacement contracts, a new five-year law enforcement agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office, and several parcel map and code update matters.
keyTopics: Appeal of the Planning Commission's denial of a 25-lot residential subdivision on Pierce Road, including its Environmental Impact Report
Five-year law enforcement services agreement with the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Office
Contracts for replacing the Bellgrove Park playground and irrigation maintenance services citywide
Purchase of electrical equipment to help electrify the Warner Hutton House, Civic Center Theater, and Joan Pisani Community Center
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for Chester Avenue and Arcadia Palms Drive

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — August 25, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered routine business including a museum roof replacement contract, an EV charger installation project at the maintenance yard, and acceptance of completed work at the Woodland Library patio. The Council also held a public hearing on a resident petition to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street, and reviewed two condominium development proposals — a 19-unit project at 349 First Street and a 33-unit project on Sherwood and Acacia Avenues.
keyTopics: Public hearing on renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Vesting tentative map for 19 condominium units at 349 First Street
Vesting tentative map for 33 condominium units at Sherwood and Acacia Avenues
Contract award for History Museum roof replacement and Maintenance Yard EV chargers project
Draft responses to Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims and BART Silicon Valley Phase II oversight

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up routine business including approval of prior meeting minutes, financial reports, and payroll registers, along with a professional services agreement and an amendment to an existing contract. The Council also considered a town code cleanup ordinance, selected a voting delegate for an upcoming League of California Cities event, and addressed a request related to a pending public hearing appeal.
keyTopics: Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026
Professional services agreement and a second amendment to an existing agreement
Omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code
Voting delegate and alternate appointment for the League of California Cities annual meeting
Request to continue or hear a public hearing appeal

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 26, 2026
san-jose.summary: This was a procedural Rules and Open Government Committee meeting focused on organizing upcoming City Council agendas rather than debating policy. The Committee reviewed the final agenda for the September 1, 2026 Council meeting and considered a VEBA Advisory Committee appointment, while the September 8 meeting was cancelled.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 1, 2026 Council meeting agenda, including possible new items and time-certain scheduling
Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 draft agenda review
Public record covering August 13–20, 2026
VEBA Advisory Committee appointment
Joint special meeting planning with the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — August 25, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council held a regular session that began with public comment on topics not otherwise on the agenda. The Council then moved into closed session to conduct a performance evaluation of two Council-appointed employees, the City Clerk and City Manager, and to discuss labor negotiations involving those two unrepresented positions.
keyTopics: Public comment period for non-agenda items
Performance evaluation of the City Clerk and City Manager
Labor negotiation discussion for the City Clerk and City Manager positions, with Vice Mayor Clark as the designated representative

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting on August 25, 2026, that began with a closed-session discussion not open to the public, followed by an evening session featuring a presentation on the CleanWater Program. No regular legislative business appears to have been on the agenda.
keyTopics: Closed session (special meeting, 4:30 p.m.)
CleanWater Program update presentation (special meeting, 6 p.m.)

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss the Bike Fest event, a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program, and a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI. The meeting also included approval of minutes from a prior session and time set aside for public comments on topics not already on the agenda.
keyTopics: Bike Fest planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Youth-led organization Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, with one councilmember, Chahal, participating remotely from India. The available agenda details focus mainly on meeting logistics rather than substantive policy items.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India
Meeting held in hybrid format with in-person and Zoom/phone options for public participation

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 11, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered an ordinance amending part of the municipal code and received an educational presentation on municipal bonds basics. The meeting also included routine items such as the council calendar, meeting minutes, and lists of upcoming and requested agenda items.
keyTopics: Ordinance introduction to amend Municipal Code Title XIII, Chapter B.6
"Municipal Bonds 101" presentation from Finance staff
City Council calendar of upcoming meetings
Approval of prior City Council meeting minutes
Preview of anticipated items for the next regular Council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Public Art Commission — August 20, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Public Art Commission considered a final design review for a public art installation planned as part of the private development at 3150 El Camino Real, with a presentation from the project's art consultant, artist, and development team. The commission also considered funding for a temporary interactive media art installation series and the acceptance of donated artworks from two local artists.
keyTopics: Final review and approval of public art plan for the 3150 El Camino Real private development, with presentation by artist Giles Miller and the Acclaim Companies development team
Allocation of up to $70,000 from the Art in Public Places CIP fund for temporary Code:ART 2027 interactive media installations
Acceptance of donated artworks by CASP artists Adrienne Defendi and Eric Fei into the city's public art collection
Approval of the June 18, 2026 Public Art Commission meeting minutes
